_readme: PUT THE SHADY AREAS HERE. One Polygon feature per unlit / avoided stretch of road.
This file is deliberately SEPARATE from zones.geojson. A fare zone answers 'where is
the rider going, and what does that cost' — it is drawn around destinations. A shady
zone answers 'what road will we not put a rider on after dark' — it is a corridor drawn
around a stretch of road. Different shapes, different reasons to change. Sharing one
polygon set means the first redraw of one silently breaks the other.
WHILE features IS EMPTY THE WHOLE FEATURE IS DORMANT: no alternatives are requested,
no toggle is offered, nothing is charged. That is intended — the safer-route option
should not appear until a real polygon exists to justify it.
HOW TO DRAW ONE
1. Open geojson.io, trace a polygon around the unlit stretch — the ROAD and a little
either side, not the whole village. A corridor roughly 300-500 m wide is right.
Too wide and safe parallel roads get flagged; too narrow and a route slips past it.
2. Copy the feature into `features` below and give it a name.
3. Set `fallback` to a lat/lng ON the Eastern Peripheral (or whichever highway the
detour should use) for this corridor — see below for when it is used.
4. Restart the backend. Zones load once at boot, same as fare zones.
COORDINATE ORDER IS [lng, lat] — GeoJSON, not the { lat, lng } used everywhere else in
the codebase. geojson.io already emits it correctly; hand-edits are where this goes wrong.
PROPERTIES
name      Shown in logs and admin only. Riders never see it — the UI says 'safer
route', never 'we think your area is unsafe'.
fallback  { lat, lng } on the highway, or null. Used ONLY when Google offers no
alternative that misses this zone: the estimate then re-asks with this point
forced as a via-waypoint. Normally unused — alternatives usually contain a
clean route already, and letting Google pick beats a coordinate we froze.
null means 'if there is no clean alternative, offer nothing' — safe default.
notes     Free text. Why this polygon exists, who reported it, when it was drawn.
EXAMPLE — delete the quotes and paste into `features`:
"type": "Feature",
"properties": {
"name": "Chithera cut",
"fallback": { "lat": 28.5, "lng": 77.5 },
"notes": "Unlit village road, shortest campus exit toward Noida. Reported by students Jul 2026."
"geometry": {
"type": "Polygon",
VERIFY BEFORE YOU TRUST IT: run `node backend/scripts/check-shady-zones.js`. It routes
campus to every fare zone and reports which destinations actually cross this polygon,
and whether a clean alternative exists for them. That is the difference between knowing
the feature works and hoping it does.
